tool_input.title: shop/api CrashLoop caused by log-shipper sidecar OOM
tool_input.content:
Cluster: kind-aurora-lab (on-prem, cluster_id kubeconfig-72ec91c49951c05d), namespace shop, deployment "api".

**Pattern:** Deployment api went from revision 1 (single "api" container, healthy) to revision 2, which added a "log-shipper" sidecar container with resources.limits.memory=16Mi, but the sidecar's command does `buf=bytearray(40*1024*1024)` on startup — 2.5x its own memory limit. Container gets OOMKilled (exit 137) within seconds of every start, kubelet enters BackOff, pod stays 1/2 Ready indefinitely, deployment never reaches MinimumAvailable -> triggers KubePodCrashLooping alert. The main "api" container itself was healthy throughout (Restart Count 0) — the crash was entirely from the sidecar.

**Why it matters:** A crash-looping sidecar can keep an otherwise-healthy pod/deployment unavailable. Don't assume the main app container is the problem just because the pod/deployment is reported unhealthy — check ALL containers in `kubectl describe pod`, not just the primary one.

**How to apply / diagnose quickly:**
1. `kubectl get pods -n <ns>` — look at READY column (e.g. "1/2") to spot partial container readiness, not just restart count.
2. `kubectl describe pod <pod>` — check every container's State/Last State/Reason/Exit Code, not just the first.
3. Compare `resources.limits.memory` against what the container's command/code actually needs/allocates.
4. Check `kubectl get replicaset -n <ns> -o wide` to see if a previous (healthy) ReplicaSet still exists as a rollback target before suggesting `kubectl rollout undo`.
5. Fix options: rollback deployment to prior revision (fast mitigation), or raise the sidecar's memory limit to match actual usage / fix the sidecar code to not over-allocate (fix-forward, addresses root cause).
tool_input.description: KubePodCrashLooping on shop/api: root cause was a log-shipper sidecar with 16Mi memory limit but code that allocates a 40MB buffer on startup, guaranteeing OOMKill every restart
